publicRelease: 1.0.5 was published from 88f8808ee66c6de733d718bd7588f96677a9da47; a version number cannot be reused, so the contract fixes shipped as 1.0.6 and then as 1.0.7, which registry.npmjs.org serves as latest with gitHead 0209e8e176e5b0fc36f6b9bd3c1fa49476370af0 and shasum 603c5fc76c5512483b0a68f3e06fb4787bb50eb4, its tarball byte-identical to npm pack at that commit

manifestCompatibilityFix.change: manifest-only: engines.dsh and dsh.compatibility.dsh moved from a single version or a 0.1.7-rc.1 floor to the range ">=0.1.7-alpha.2 <0.2.0", dsh.compatibility.node added ">=22.19.0", and dshReleases plus dshOperations now declare every release in the live latest-three window: 0.1.7-alpha.2, 0.1.7-rc.1 and 0.1.7-rc.2
manifestCompatibilityFix.windowAuthority: official-dsh-releases.mjs resolves the latest-three window from official GitHub Releases and published npm versions in the active major.minor line; previews tagged on the next channel that belong to a later major.minor line are deliberately excluded
manifestCompatibilityFix.runtimeEvidenceCarriesForward: for 1.0.7 itself: lib/index.js and client/client.js were byte-identical to 1.0.6, so the end-to-end evidence in the matrix above applies to that release unchanged
manifestCompatibilityFix.undeclared: a release that has not been tested stays undeclared rather than being claimed, so it reads as unknown; peer dependencies still pin 0.1.7-rc.1
manifestCompatibilityFix.method: each release ran against its own @deepseek-ai/dsh CLI in a throwaway DSH_HOME: profile 'acceptance' built from the shipped web template, dsh-worktree-space-1.0.7.tgz installed, --dump-config composed the worktree-space row, cold start printed its URL with no warning, the page carried dsh-worktree-space/client.js with the plugin RPC answering ok:true, then remove dropped the package and left zero occurrences, and a second cold start was clean

observations.pnpmPeerNotice: the routine '[WARN] Issues with peer dependencies found' appears in every install, including the already-verified 0.1.7-rc.2; it is not a version incompatibility

archiveStrategyRelease.change: the archived-documents root became a configured strategy instead of one computed rule: dsh.compatibility.dshOperations is untouched, but the finish dialog now chooses between a fixed anchor on the task container's volume (<volume>\worktree-space\archived-docs, the new default), the container beside the task space (<container>\archived-docs, the previous behaviour) and a configured directory, and adds the per-task <workspace>-<stamp> folder under whichever root is in force
archiveStrategyRelease.hostContractUnchanged: the Host side of the archive is the same surface: task.done still carries the same documentsDirectory string, finishTask still validates it with assertIsolated against the task container, and archive.js's copy/clean-up paths are unchanged. The Host plugin gains one configuration field and one accessor, and lib/index.js is rebuilt for it.
archiveStrategyRelease.clientBundleChanged: client/client.js is no longer byte-identical to 1.0.6 or 1.0.7 - it now computes the destination from the served strategy - so the byte-identity claim recorded under manifestCompatibilityFix stops at 1.0.7
archiveStrategyRelease.lifecycleRowsNotReRun: not yet run for 1.0.8: the install/start/uninstall/rollback rows in the matrix above were taken against 1.0.6 and 1.0.7 tarballs and have not been repeated against a published 1.0.8. The three roots are covered by unit tests (test/documents.test.ts) and by the finish-dialog tests (test/task-finish.test.tsx) only so far; the disposable-profile matrix should be re-run before 1.0.8 is offered to the Catalog
archiveStrategyRelease.dumpConfigCountsMayMove: the --dump-config line counts recorded above are 1.0.7's; a release that adds a configuration field may compose a different tree, so those numbers must not be carried into a 1.0.8 claim without measuring again
